aboutMe: I am completing a B.S. in Statistics at Guangzhou University and have been admitted to Shenzhen University's M.S. program in Applied Statistics through its recommendation-based admission process.

My research interests span AI for Science (AI4S), AI for Statistics, high-dimensional statistical inference, and interval estimation. I am particularly interested in AI-assisted scientific computing, GPU-based statistical simulations, and the validation of computational results.

My research has focused on power-enhanced tests for high-dimensional two-sample Behrens–Fisher problems, prior-free interval estimation for constrained parameters, and exact interval estimation for Poisson signals with unknown backgrounds.

work.name: Power-Enhanced Tests for the High-Dimensional Two-Sample Behrens–Fisher Problem
work.summary: Developed power-enhanced Cauchy combination tests for high-dimensional two-sample inference under sparse, dense, and scale-heterogeneous signals.
responsibilities: Integrated Welch's t-tests with the Cauchy combination method to develop WCCT, then proposed EWCCT and EWCCTS to address sparse, dense, and scale-heterogeneous signals.
Designed simulation studies and real-data analyses to compare the proposed methods with existing approaches in terms of Type I error control and empirical power.
The proposed methods maintained Type I error control, while EWCCTS achieved competitive empirical power.
Led the conception of the methods, theoretical derivations, experimental design, result analysis, and initial manuscript drafting.

work.name: Prior-Free Probabilistic Interval Estimation for Constrained Parameters
work.summary: Developed prior-free interval estimation methods based on inferential models for constrained normal and Poisson means with nuisance parameters.
responsibilities: For normal means, IM achieved exact coverage, with intervals slightly longer than those from Bayesian methods. For Poisson means, IM was conservative, whereas NIM coverage was closest to the nominal level.
Led method implementation and the analyses of neutrino-mass and signal-intensity data, and drafted the initial manuscript.

work.name: Exact Confidence Intervals for Poisson Signals with Unknown Background
work.summary: Developed an exact confidence-interval method for Poisson signals with unknown backgrounds by combining the h-function, Poisson-quantile truncation, and the Berger–Boos correction.
responsibilities: Compared interval coverage and length through simulation studies and analyzed KARMEN neutrino-detection data.
Led the simulations, method implementation, efficiency optimization, and initial manuscript drafting.

projects.name: SimForge-GPU: AI-Assisted GPU Migration and Validation for Statistical Simulations
projects.description: A local GPU migration tool for AI coding assistants and statistical simulation programs. It analyzes a script and creates a conversion plan, then conservatively rewrites supported CPU code to run on a GPU. It also reports unsupported features, validation results, and benchmark results.
